explain.say: The female lays one egg and carefully passes it to the male, then walks back to the sea to feed. The father balances the egg on his feet under a warm fold of skin, the brood pouch, for about two months, eating nothing.

explain.say: Thousands of males huddle together, shuffling slowly so every bird gets turns in the warm middle and on the windy edge. Even so, by the time the females return, fathers have lost up to around 40 percent of their weight.

explain.say: The mothers return just as the chicks hatch, bringing food in their stomachs, and then the parents take turns fishing. Older chicks gather in groups for warmth, and by summer they grow waterproof feathers and head out to sea.

faq.q: Why do emperor penguin fathers hold the eggs?
faq.a: Making the egg uses up much of the female's reserves, so she must go to sea to feed. The male, who built up fat before the breeding season, can fast while keeping the egg warm on his feet.
asks: Do male penguins look after eggs?

faq.a: Huddling cuts the body surface each bird exposes to the wind and cold, so it uses far less energy. The inside of a huddle can rise above 20 degrees Celsius, and slow shuffling lets birds take turns in the middle.
asks: How do penguins stay warm in winter?
How warm is a penguin huddle?

faq.q: Why do emperor penguins breed in winter?
faq.a: Their chicks take many months to grow. Starting in winter means the chicks are ready to go to sea in summer, when food is plentiful and the sea ice breaks up.
asks: Why lay eggs in the coldest season?

faq.q: What does a penguin chick eat?
faq.a: Its parents bring back fish, krill and squid in their stomachs and bring it up into the chick's mouth. If the mother is late, the father can feed the newly hatched chick a milky substance from his throat.
asks: How do penguins feed their babies?

faq.q: How is climate change affecting emperor penguins?
faq.a: Emperor penguins need stable sea ice until their chicks are ready for the sea. In some recent years the ice broke up too early in parts of Antarctica, and whole colonies of chicks were lost.
asks: Why does sea ice matter to penguins?

facts: Male emperor penguins can go about four months without eating through courtship and incubation.
Temperatures inside an emperor penguin huddle can rise above 20 °C (Gilbert and colleagues, 2006).
